item.title: Fiji beaten by Mongolia in FIBA Asia Cup 2029 Pre-Qualifiers
item.description: Fiji has suffered a heavy 102–40 defeat to Mongolia in the first round of the FIBA Asia Cup 2029 Pre-Qualifiers . The Fiji men’s basketball side struggled against a strong Mongolian outfit, with Mongolia securing a 62-point victory.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji has suffered a heavy 102–40 defeat to Mongolia in the first round of the FIBA Asia Cup 2029 Pre-Qualifiers .

The Fiji men’s basketball side struggled against a strong Mongolian outfit, with Mongolia securing a 62-point victory.

Basketball Fiji describes it as a tough outing for the boys , but says the team’s hopes remain high with another match still to come.

Fiji will face Vietnam at 8pm tonight in its next match of the tournament.

The team will be looking to bounce back strongly and finish the first round on a positive note .

item.title: Bati aiming to beat Australia and New Zealand - coach
item.description: Temalesi Vono , Alipate Narawa · 31/08/2026 Fiji has been drawn alongside the two rugby league giants in the pool stage, but Potter says the Bati will not be travelling merely to compete.
item.content:encoded:
Temalesi Vono , Alipate Narawa · 31/08/2026

Fiji has been drawn alongside the two rugby league giants in the pool stage, but Potter says the Bati will not be travelling merely to compete.

The Bati squad is also expected to spend time in Fiji before heading to Australia, with Potter saying the focus will be on cultural integration rather than training.

The squad will spend about six days in Fiji before travelling to Newcastle, where they will arrive a week before their first match.

Potter says he will return to Australia and visit as many players as possible to assess their physical condition and mentality ahead of the tournament.

The Bati are pooled with defending champions Australia, New Zealand and the Cook Islands at the Rugby League World Cup, which kicks off on October 15th, 2026 and is hosted by Australia, New Zealand, and Papua New Guinea.

item.title: Local players not currently on Fiji Bati coach Mick Potter’s radar
item.description: Local players are currently not on Vodafone Fiji Bati coach Mick Porter's radar. Porter told the media that he has been watching some of the local competitions, but local players are currently not on his radar for Bati selection.
item.content:encoded:
Local players are currently not on Vodafone Fiji Bati coach Mick Porter's radar.

Porter told the media that he has been watching some of the local competitions, but local players are currently not on his radar for Bati selection.

He says local players need to be part of an elite system, as this would help them become as well prepared as players competing at higher levels.

Porter says he has a lot of respect for Fiji's local players and believes there will come a time when they elevate their game to the standard required to play for the Bati.

With 45 days to go until the Rugby League World Cup, Porter says they have not finalised their squad yet, but they have a good idea of the players they want in it.

The Bati are pooled with defending champions Australia, New Zealand and the Cook Islands at the Rugby League World Cup, which kicks off on October 15th, 2026.

item.title: Silktails players to build financial skills through Westpac partnership
item.description: Kaiviti Silktails players will now have the opportunity to build their financial skills alongside their rugby league careers through a new programme with Westpac Fiji. The initiative will see Westpac Fiji open bank accounts for all Silktails players and provide financial literacy training to players and staff.
item.content:encoded:
Kaiviti Silktails players will now have the opportunity to build their financial skills alongside their rugby league careers through a new programme with Westpac Fiji.

The initiative will see Westpac Fiji open bank accounts for all Silktails players and provide financial literacy training to players and staff.

Westpac Fiji says the training will cover practical areas such as budgeting, saving, financial planning and managing money, with the aim of giving players greater confidence in making financial decisions.

Kaiviti Silktails Rugby League Football Club Chairman Petero Civoniceva says the programme is about developing players as people, not only as athletes.

He says access to banking support and financial training will be an important part of preparing players for life both on and off the field.

The partnership will also extend to primary school students through the CatchPassProgram, with Westpac Fiji and the Kaiviti Silktails set to visit primary schools across Fiji.

The visits will combine rugby league activities with simple, age-appropriate financial education sessions to help children understand money and develop good financial habits from an early age.

Westpac Head of Corporate Affairs, Marketing and Community Rachel White says the partnership provides Westpac with a practical way to support young Fijians through sport and education.

She says the financial education component will give players practical skills that can benefit them now and in the future.

The partnership will also see Westpac sponsor the Monthly Westpac Values Clubman Award.

The financial literacy sessions form part of the broader Westpac Fiji and Kaiviti Silktails partnership, which was launched earlier this year.

Westpac Pacific’s Financial Literacy programme has been running since 2013 and has trained more than 100,000 people across schools, communities and businesses in Fiji and Papua New Guinea.

The free programme provides education, resources and tools covering areas such as budgeting, saving, financial planning, income and expenses, and money management at different stages of life.

Through the new partnership, Silktails players and young students will now have access to these skills as they develop both on and off the rugby league field.

item.title: Cricket Fiji boosts coaching development with two new ICC Tutors
item.description: Two Cricket Fiji staff members Joeli Mateyawa Seuvou and Vulisere Waqavakatoga have taken an important step in their coaching careers after successfully completing the 2026 ICC East Asia Pacific Level 1 Coach Tutor Course in Brisbane, Australia. The Cricket Fiji Development Manager and Development Officer completed the three-day course earlier this month and are now recognised as ICC Tutors.
item.content:encoded:
Two Cricket Fiji staff members Joeli Mateyawa Seuvou and Vulisere Waqavakatoga have taken an important step in their coaching careers after successfully completing the 2026 ICC East Asia Pacific Level 1 Coach Tutor Course in Brisbane, Australia.

The Cricket Fiji Development Manager and Development Officer completed the three-day course earlier this month and are now recognised as ICC Tutors.

The course focused on preparing participants to train, develop and support coaches in their respective countries.

Seuvou says the programme had given him and Waqavakatoga a better understanding of how to develop coaches and, more importantly, how to teach and support them effectively.

He says they could now bring the knowledge gained from the course back to Fiji and use it to help strengthen the country's coaching system.

As ICC Tutors, Seuvou and Waqavakatoga will support Cricket Fiji in developing more quality coaches and delivering ICC-recognised coaching programmes locally.

The ICC Training and Education programme provides structured learning pathways for coaches, umpires, scorers and pitch curators around the world, with a key focus on helping Associate Members build their own trained and accredited workforce.

Cricket Fiji CEO Anushil Kumar says the organisation was grateful to ICC East Asia Pacific for providing the opportunity to Seuvou and Waqavakatoga.

Kumar says Cricket Fiji would continue to prioritise the professional development of its staff across different areas, as investing in its people would help strengthen the workforce, improve programme delivery and create more opportunities for the growth of cricket in Fiji.

The next step will be for Cricket Fiji and its newly recognised Tutors to work with ICC East Asia Pacific on a country plan and identify the next priorities for coach education and development in Fiji.

The appointment of Seuvou and Waqavakatoga as ICC Tutors will give Cricket Fiji additional capacity to build a stronger and more sustainable coaching system from the grassroots level upwards.
